about.title: Oakdale Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Oakdale sees a steady stream of injury collisions each year, with public records showing 75 such crashes and 109 injured people in the latest final count. Traffic tends to bunch up on Friday afternoons between noon and 2 p.m., and corridors like E F Street, W F Street, and S Yosemite Avenue see their share of reported crashes. When a collision happens here, in Stanislaus County, the aftermath can feel overwhelming — medical appointments, missed work, and calls from insurance adjusters all at once. LawProactive isn't a law firm; we're a free service that connects injured people with an independent personal injury attorney who works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery. The sooner evidence is preserved after a crash, the stronger a claim tends to be, so reaching out early matters.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Talking to the Insurer

items.title: California's Two-Year Deadline Is Firm
items.desc: Under California law, you generally have two years from the crash date to file a lawsuit, though claims against a government entity can require notice in as little as six months. Missing that window can end your ability to recover anything.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Cut Into Your Recovery
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning your compensation can be reduced by whatever percentage of blame you're assigned — even if that's just talk from an insurance adjuster. An attorney can push back on unfair fault assignments before they take hold.

items.title: No Cap Means Your Full Story Matters
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, so a well-documented account of how the crash affected your daily life can matter. Avoiding a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer helps keep that story in your control, not theirs.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's usually best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to minimize your claim later. An independent attorney can advise you on what, if anything, to share.

items.question: What if my accident happened at a Friday afternoon rush near S Yosemite Avenue or E F Street?
items.answer: Reported crashes in Oakdale tend to peak on Fridays between noon and 2 p.m., often along corridors like S Yosemite Avenue and E F Street. Timing and location can affect witness availability and traffic camera footage, so it helps to have evidence preserved quickly. An attorney can help track down these details before they're lost.

items.question: How much does it cost to work with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: LawProactive's connection service is free, and attorneys in our network typically work on contingency. That means there's no upfront fee, and payment only comes if there's a recovery in your case.
